tech_stack: C# / ASP.NET Core 6, SQL Server (Dapper + raw ADO.NET), Kafka (SharedEventBus Avro), Azure Blob Storage, New Relic, LaunchDarkly

domains.name: File & Versioning
domains.responsibility: Manages the full lifecycle of content files and their versions, including upload, checkout/checkin, metadata updates, variants, renditions, and extension policies.
domains.health_reason: FileManager and FileVersionManager are one-method pass-through shells; all lifecycle invariants (checkout ownership, publishability, permission checks) live in FileWriter/PublishWriter in the application layer.
key_operations: FileActionController (checkout, checkin, copy, move, rename, delete)

invariants: A file can only be checked out by one user at a time
Only the checked-out user (or a full-control admin) may check it back in
A file whose type is non-publishable cannot enter the publish workflow
File extension determines allowed rendition types

domains.name: Folder & Library Structure
domains.responsibility: Owns the hierarchical library tree of folders including shortcuts, materialized paths, and team-site root bindings.
domains.health_reason: FolderRepository contains correct logic but executes raw SQL (SqlParameter/SqlConnection) directly in the domain class, violating infrastructure separation.

invariants: A shortcut folder's OriginLink must point to an existing non-deleted primary folder
A folder cannot be moved into one of its own descendants
Deleting a folder cascades deletion to all descendant content

domains.name: Content Publishing & Approval
domains.responsibility: Orchestrates the publish, promote, activate, schedule-publish, review/approval, and SBP (state-based publishing) workflow for content files.
domains.health_reason: Business invariants around publishability and checkout state are validated inside PublishWriter/ActivationWriter (application layer) rather than in a domain object; no domain events are raised on publish to signal downstream consumers.

invariants: A non-publishable content type (folder, shortcut) cannot be published
A file checked out by another user cannot be published
Scheduled publish date must be in the future
Publish removes any existing schedule-publish tasks for the same file

domains.name: Content Permissions & Access Control
domains.responsibility: Manages unique (item-level) permissions, granular permission settings, and permission inheritance for content objects and folders within team sites.
domains.health_reason: ContentPermissionManager exists but batch-permission writes and unique-permission validation run directly in PermissionWriter with inline Dapper queries, bypassing the domain manager.

invariants: An item with inherited permissions must derive them from its nearest ancestor with unique permissions
Unique permissions require at least one owner
Removing unique permissions resets the item to inherited

domains.name: Team Site
domains.responsibility: Owns team site entities, their member rosters, and team-site-scoped activity tracking; acts as the primary organizational container for library content.
domains.health_reason: TeamSiteMemberManager and TeamSiteReader exist but TeamSiteWriter has direct Dapper SQL for membership operations rather than routing through the domain manager.

invariants: A team site must have at least one owner-level member
Content can only reside in one primary team site
Member role changes propagate inherited permissions to the team site root folder

domains.name: Custom Properties
domains.responsibility: Manages custom property schema definitions and their values on content objects; processes property-change jobs triggered by schema updates.
domains.health_reason: CustomPropertyManager is a thin coordinator; business rules for XML property resolution and change propagation are scattered across CustomPropertyXmlResolver, PropertyMessageController (Express Executor), and CustomPropertyBackgroundService.

invariants: Property values must conform to the type defined in the property schema
Hidden properties cannot be set by end users
Schema changes enqueue propagation jobs for all affected content objects

domains.name: Content Expiration
domains.responsibility: Enforces expiration policies on file versions, sends expiration notifications, and manages expiration refresh and bulk-expire operations.
domains.health_reason: ExpirationWriter contains multi-step business logic (batch expire, notification dispatch) that belongs in a domain service; no domain aggregate enforces expiration invariants.

invariants: Expiration date must be in the future when set
A version cannot be expired if it is the only published version with active profile assignments
Notification users must have read access to the content

domains.name: External Content Sync
domains.responsibility: Manages synchronization of library content with external cloud storage providers (Google Drive, OneDrive) and ECM systems, including task tracking, credential management, and migration pipelines.
domains.health_reason: ExternalSyncManager and ContentSyncManager exist but ExternalSyncWriter has raw Dapper queries; ECM migration steps (ECMMigrationRunnerService, FinalizeMigrationStep) contain orchestration logic that belongs in a domain service.

invariants: Only one active sync task may run per external folder mapping at a time
Sync credentials must be refreshed before expiry
ECM migration dry-run must pass before full migration is committed

domains.name: Content Activity & Analytics
domains.responsibility: Records content view events, user activity, sharing, live insights reports, data collection, annotations, comments, ask-expert interactions, and publishes analytics events to downstream consumers.
domains.health_reason: ContentViewWriter/ContentViewReader contain inline business-logic (pin limits, view limits, filter mutation) and direct Dapper queries; there is no domain model for ContentView — it is treated as a data bag manipulated entirely in the application layer.

invariants: A user may not have more than the tenant-configured maximum pinned views
Total content views per user may not exceed the system limit
A standard (system-generated) view name may not be reused for a custom view

domains.name: SBP Profile & Workspace
domains.responsibility: Manages content workspaces (Profiles / Programs) that serve as publish destinations, including SBP profile file processing and profile-version lifecycle.
domains.health_reason: ProfileRepository is a direct SQL repository; SBPProfileWriter delegates to external SBP SDK with no domain invariants enforced locally; profile-version existence is validated via Checkpoints in the orchestrator layer rather than in a domain object.

invariants: A profile must have at least one active version
Content can only be assigned to a profile the user has access to
SBP profiles require a published version before content assignment

domains.name: MicroApp & LiveDoc
domains.responsibility: Manages Tiled MicroApp and LiveDoc interactive content types including their creation, editing, metadata, and integration with the Tiled external service.
domains.health_reason: MicroAppManager exists but MicroApp add/edit flows are routed through ExtensiveFileWriter (a generic application-layer writer) rather than a dedicated domain service; Tiled service coupling is in TiledClient inside the domain project with no interface abstraction at the domain boundary.

invariants: A MicroApp version under active editing cannot be published until editing session is closed
LiveDoc content must reference a valid HTML host page
MicroApp tile configuration must be fetched from Tiled service before publishing

domains.name: System & Configuration
domains.responsibility: Manages tenant-scoped system settings, app configuration, feature toggles, system identities (users/groups), item types, and refresh-cache operations.
domains.health_reason: AppConfigurationManager provides a clean manager layer over AppConfigurationRepository; FeatureToggleService delegates to LaunchDarkly without leaking infrastructure; SystemIdentityManager manages user/group lookups consistently.

invariants: Configuration keys are unique per tenant
Feature toggle state is read-only from domain perspective (governed by LaunchDarkly)
System identity users are tenant-scoped and cannot be shared across tenants

steps.label: PublishWriter — validate file is publishable and not checked out by another user
ScheduleActivateBackgroundService — activates content at scheduled time
SyncIndicatorBGService — poll external provider for changes
FileWriter.AddFile or UpdateFile per synced item
PropertyMessageController — queue changes per team site
Unpublish expired version from all profiles
CMServiceClient — fetch source content via ECM API
ExtensiveFileWriter.AddMicroApp — create file record + tiled metadata
TiledClient — register tile config with Tiled service
PublishWriter.PublishFile — publish after editing is closed
ContentViewReader / ContentQueryReader — apply filters, custom property filters
FlexibleContentQueryReader — raw Dapper SQL query against ContentObject
SearchMesh ingest event for indexed content

gap_analysis.title: Checkout invariant lives in application layer
ContentView business rules in application writer
Direct Dapper SQL in application-layer Readers and Writers
FolderRepository executes raw ADO.NET SQL inline
IsNonPublishableType check duplicated across two writers
No domain events raised on publish or expiration
gap_analysis.detail:
FilePublished and FileVersionExpired are significant state transitions that downstream services (search, analytics, profile caching) need to react to, yet they produce only a generic Kafka ContentEvent with a type flag rather than typed domain events. PublishWriter builds the event payload inline (strings, dictionaries) rather than using a named domain event class. This makes the contract implicit and fragile.

After: Introduce FilePublishedEvent, FileVersionExpiredEvent domain event types in Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Abstractions.Events.Model, raised by the domain aggregate and dispatched by the application layer.

gap_analysis.title: TiledClient has no domain interface
gap_analysis.detail: TiledClient in Seismic.ContentManager.Domain/MicroApp/TiledClient.cs is a concrete HTTP client registered directly; MicroAppManager depends on it by concrete type. The domain project should depend on an ITiledClient interface so the Tiled integration can be stubbed in tests and swapped without touching domain logic.

gap_analysis.title: CustomPropertyXmlResolver contains parsing + validation logic outside aggregate
gap_analysis.detail: CustomPropertyXmlResolver and CustomPropertyDefinitionResolver in the domain project parse XML property definitions and resolve values, but they are standalone helpers rather than methods on the CustomPropertyDefinitionModel aggregate root. Property schema validation should be an invariant of the aggregate, not a utility class called from the manager.

gap_analysis.title: ProfileRepository is a plain SQL repository with no domain behaviour
gap_analysis.detail: ProfileRepository contains only data-access methods; all profile-related business logic (version existence, SBP eligibility) is validated via Checkpoints in the orchestration layer (ProfileVersionExistanceCheckpoint, ProfileExistanceCheckpoint). These are domain invariants that belong on ProfileModel rather than on infrastructure checkpoints.
